137

143                 input_payload=payload["input"],

157                 status=payload.get("status", "succeeded"),
158                 settlement=payload.get("settlement"),
159             )
160         except ValueError as exc:
161             # An issuance the plugin would itself reject is a client error, and the reason
162             # code in the message is the whole point of SPEC.md §11.2 — do not swallow it.
163             raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(exc))
164 
165         storage.store(receipt)
166         logger.info("AWR/2 provenance receipt created: %s", receipt.receipt_id)

169     @router.get("/receipt/{receipt_id:path}")
170     async def get_receipt(
171         receipt_id: str,
172         origin: str = Header(default=""),
173     ) -> JSONResponse:
174         """Retrieve an immutable AWR document with narrow, GET-only CORS.
175 
176         The verifier and USE portal need to fetch this public document in the
177         caller's browser.  Adding those origins to the hub-wide CORS middleware
178         would also authorize cross-origin POSTs to state-changing routes.  The
179         receipt endpoint therefore emits ACAO itself only for the two explicit
180         read surfaces; every other origin can still navigate to the public JSON
181         but cannot read it from script.
182         """
183         receipt = storage.get_by_receipt_id(receipt_id)
184         if not receipt:
185             raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Receipt not found")
186         headers = {
187             "Cache-Control": "public, max-age=31536000, immutable",
188             "Vary": "Origin",
189             "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff",
190         }
191         if origin in allowed_receipt_origins:
192             headers["Access-Control-Allow-Origin"] = origin
193         return JSONResponse(
194             content=receipt.to_dict(),
195             headers=headers,
196             media_type="application/vc+ld+json",
197         )
198 
199     @router.get("/verify/{receipt_id:path}")
200     async def verify(receipt_id: str, profile: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
201         """Verify a provenance receipt by ID — all checks (public)."""
202         receipt = storage.get_by_receipt_id(receipt_id)
203         if not receipt:
204             raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Receipt not found")
205 
206         # Bind this hub's own identity to its signing key: a stored receipt that claims to
207         # be issued by us must carry our real key. Under AWR/2 the key is derived from
208         # `issuer.id`, so the pin is on the did:key itself (SPEC.md §5.1).
209         try:
210             own_did = did_key_for_signer(signer)
211         except Exception as exc:  # a broken key file must not 500 a public GET
212             logger.error("cannot derive this hub's did:key: %s", exc)
213             own_did = ""
214         pins = {hub_name: signer.public_key_b64}
215         if own_did:
216             pins[own_did] = signer.public_key_b64
217 
218         # §8.2: chain edges are resolved only against documents the caller supplied — a
219         # verifier MUST NOT fetch a parent. These come out of this hub's own storage,
220         # which is not the network, and an edge whose parent is absent stays `unresolved`,
221         # which is not an error.
222         parents = [
223             parent
224             for parent in (
225                 storage.get_by_receipt_id(pid) for pid in receipt.parent_receipts
226             )
227             if parent is not None
228         ]
229 
230         result = verify_receipt(
231             receipt,
232             trusted_issuer_keys=pins,
233             parents=parents or None,
234             profile=profile,
235         )
236         return {
237             "receipt_id": receipt_id,
238             "model_id": receipt.model_id,
239             "provider_hub": receipt.provider_hub,
240             "timestamp": receipt.timestamp,
241             "awr_version": receipt.awr_version,
242             "issuer": receipt.issuer_id,
243             "cryptosuite": receipt.cryptosuite or None,
244             "format": "AWR/1 (legacy, verify-only)" if receipt.is_legacy else "AWR/2",
245             "verifier": {"awr_version": AWR_VERSION, "cryptosuite": CRYPTOSUITE},
246             **result.to_dict(),
247         }
248 
249     return router

459 # HISTOR snapshot {day}: what MCP servers advertise, and when it changes
460 
461 HISTOR reads the tool list (`tools/list`) of every remote MCP server in the official MCP registry
462 on a polling schedule, and of npm/PyPI MCP packages run in a sandbox once per published version (new versions
463 first, a few hundred a day). It records the exact tool definitions,
464 pins them by digest, and writes a signed label to a public RFC 9162 Merkle log whenever a tool set
465 first appears, stays the same, or changes. This snapshot is that record as files.
466 
467 - **{c['listed']:,}** listed servers ({c['remote']:,} remote endpoints, {c['packages']:,} packages), plus {c['delisted']:,} delisted
468 - **{c['pinned']:,}** with a recorded tool set; **{c['everChanged']:,}** changed at least once
469 - **{f['changes.jsonl.gz']['rows']:,}** recorded changes, {(m.get('changesFrom') or '—')[:10]} to {(m.get('changesUntil') or '—')[:10]}
470 - **{f['toolsets.jsonl.gz']['rows']:,}** distinct tool sets (current ones and every one a change replaced)
471 - **{c['blockTier']:,}** servers with a block-tier WARDEN pattern match, **{c['adviseOnly']:,}** advise-only
472 
473 Live view and per-server pages: {m['source']} · code: {m['code']}
474 
475 ## Files
476 
477 | File | Rows | Size | SHA-256 |
478 | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
479 {rows}
480 
481 `manifest.json` holds the full hashes and the counts, signed by the log's key `{m['log']}`
482 (type `{DATASET_TYPE}`, Ed25519 over RFC 8785 JSON). It also carries the signed tree head the
483 export started under (tree size {head.get('treeSize', 0):,}), so any label id below can be checked
484 against the live log with `GET {m['source']}/api/v1/labels/<id>/proof`.
485 
486 ## Fields
487 
488 Fields whose shape varies between servers are JSON text (`*Json`), so every file loads as a flat
489 table. Digests are SRI strings (`sha256-…`) over the RFC 8785 form of the value.
490 
491 - **servers** — `id` (stable per name+endpoint), `name`, `title`, `description`, `endpoint`
492   (`https://…` or `npm:`/`pypi:` for packages), `transport`, `registry`, `version`, `repository`,
493   `firstListed`/`lastListed`, `delisted`, `skipReason` (why it was not dialled), `lastStatus` and
494   `lastDetail` (the last attempt's outcome), `lastObserved`, `toolCount`, `toolSetDigest` (join to
495   toolsets), `firstPinned`, `unchangedSince`, `attempts`, `observations`, `changes`,
496   `blockMatches`/`adviseMatches`/`recordMatches`, `classifierFlags`, `chainLabel` (latest label id), `page`.
497 - **toolsets** — `digest`, `toolsJson`: per tool the four members the digest covers, as served
498   (`name`, `description`, `inputSchema`, and `outputSchema` when sent).{_extras_fields(f)}
499 - **changes** — `serverId`, `observedAt`, `fromToolSetDigest` → `toToolSetDigest`, `summaryJson`
500   (tools added, removed and changed, with the field that moved), `labelId` (the signed continuity label).{_package_change_fields(f)}{_version_change_fields(m)}
501 - **scans** — `toolSetDigest`, `patternSet`, `matchesJson` (rule code, tier, severity, tool, where).
502   The rules are in `pattern-set.json`. A match is a pattern hit to look at, not a verdict.
503 - **classifications** — `toolSetDigest`, `model`, `verdictJson`: an LLM's advisory reading of the
504   tool set. Not reproducible, so it never enters the signed log.{_package_observation_fields(f)}
505 
506 ## How a change is counted
507 
508 - **What is compared.** Per tool, the members in `toolsets`: `name`, `description`, `inputSchema`, and
509   `outputSchema` when the server sent one. Tools are sorted by name and the set is hashed in its RFC 8785
510   form, so tool order, object key order and JSON whitespace never make a change. Strings are compared as
511   sent (a description that only gains a space is a change), and so is the order of arrays inside a schema
512   (`required`, `enum`). Other members (`title`, `annotations`, `_meta`, `icons`) are not in the digest;
513   {_extras_counting(f)}
514 - **When.** A change is a successful read whose digest differs from the server's previous successful
515   read. Remote polling cadence depends on the observer configuration and available capacity; packages are read
516   once per published version. States between polls can be missed. Every recorded change is
517   recorded, including one that goes back to a list the server showed before.
518 - **Failed reads.** A timeout, an HTTP error, a server that asks for credentials or one HISTOR does not
519   dial is never a change: the server keeps its last list, and `lastStatus` says how the last attempt
520   went. A server that never answered without credentials has no tool set.
521 - **One client.** HISTOR reads without credentials, from one host. Lists that differ by user, account or
522   region are not seen; a list that differs per session shows up as changes alternating between two digests.
523 - **What moved.** In `summaryJson`, a modified tool names the members that moved: `description` as a
524   word diff, `inputSchema`/`outputSchema` as JSON paths (a parameter description is a path ending in
525   `"description"`). A renamed tool is a removal plus an addition. `detail` is `names-only` when one side
526   could not be digested; that change compares names only.
527

529 
530 ```python
531 import pandas as pd
532 servers = pd.read_json("servers.jsonl.gz", lines=True)
533 changes = pd.read_json("changes.jsonl.gz", lines=True)
534 ```

537 -- DuckDB
538 SELECT name, count(*) AS changes FROM 'changes.jsonl.gz' c
539 JOIN 'servers.jsonl.gz' s ON s.id = c.serverId GROUP BY name ORDER BY changes DESC LIMIT 20;
540 
541 -- Changes in which nothing moved but tool descriptions
542 SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT summaryJson::JSON AS s FROM 'changes.jsonl.gz')
543 WHERE s->>'detail' = 'full' AND json_array_length(s->'added') = 0 AND json_array_length(s->'removed') = 0
544   AND json_array_length(s->'modified') > 0
545   AND list_bool_and(list_transform(from_json(s->'modified', '["JSON"]'), m -> json_keys(m->'fields') = ['description']));
546 ```
547 
548 `scripts/change_kinds.py` in the code repository sorts every change by the fields it touched.
549 
550 ## What it is not
551 
552 - A tool list is what a server advertised to an anonymous client on that day. Servers that need
553   credentials, or that refused HISTOR, have no tool set here (`lastStatus`, `skipReason` say why).
554 - Pattern matches and classifier flags point at text worth reading; they do not say a server is malicious.
555 - A change is a change in the definitions, not a judgement of it. Most are ordinary releases.
